Content:
In isosceles right triangles such as the one shown below, the angles always measure [MATH: 45^\circ,] [MATH: 45^\circ,] and [MATH: 90^\circ.]

Content:
Consequently, isosceles right triangles are often called [MATH: \boldsymbol{45^\circ}]-[MATH: \boldsymbol{45^\circ}]-[MATH: \boldsymbol{90^\circ}] triangles.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/426bb4e3743bd646d6c1d9cc5b309421]

Content:
All [MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 90^\circ] triangles share a special property:

Content:
> In any [MATH: {45^\circ}]-[MATH: {45^\circ}]-[MATH: {90^\circ}] triangle, the length of the hypotenuse is [MATH: \sqrt{2}] times the length of a leg.

Content:
To see why this is, remember that

Content:
- in an isosceles triangle, the two legs must have the same length, and
- in a right triangle, the square of the longest side must equal the sum of the squares of the two shorter sides.

Content:
So, if an isosceles right triangle has legs of length [MATH: a] and the hypotenuse has length [MATH: h,] then we have

Content:
[MATH: h^{2}|= a^{2} + a^{2}; h^{2}|= 2a^{2}; h|= sqrt(2a^{2}); h|= sqrt(2) ⋅ a.]

sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The hypotenuse in a [MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 90^\circ] triangle is equal to [MATH: \sqrt{2}] times the length of a leg.

Here, we know that the hypotenuse has length [MATH: 5.] So, if the length of a leg is [MATH: a,] then we must have

[MATH: 5|= sqrt(2) ⋅ a; a|= (5)/(sqrt(2)).]

To remove the square root from the denominator, we can multiply both the numerator and denominator by [MATH: \sqrt{2},] as follows:

[MATH: a|= (5 ⋅ sqrt(2))/(sqrt(2) ⋅ sqrt(2)); a|= (5sqrt(2))/(2)]

Therefore, the length of each leg is [MATH: \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}.]

sections.normalized_html: The perimeter of the triangle below is [MATH: 26+13\sqrt{2}.] Find the measure of the hypotenuse.
sections.readable_text:
The perimeter of the triangle below is [MATH: 26+13\sqrt{2}.] Find the measure of the hypotenuse.

[IMG: /graphics/18eee045d8e3960ccc136b868ba3a6a1]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Because the triangle is isosceles, the legs must have the same length. Let [MATH: a] be the length of each leg. So, we have

[MATH: AB=BC=a.]

Moreover, because the triangle is a right isosceles triangle, the hypotenuse must be equal to [MATH: \sqrt{2}] times the length of a leg. Therefore, [MATH: AC = AB\cdot\sqrt{2} = a\sqrt{2}.]

Finally, since the perimeter is [MATH: p = 26+13\sqrt{2},] we have

[MATH: p|= AB + BC + AC; 26 + 13sqrt(2)|= a + a + asqrt(2); 26 + 13sqrt(2)|= 2a + asqrt(2); 13(2 + sqrt(2))|= a(2 + sqrt(2)); 13(2 + sqrt(2))|= a(2 + sqrt(2)); 13|= a.]

Therefore, the length of each leg is [MATH: a=13,] and the length of the hypotenuse is

[MATH: AC = a \sqrt{2} = 13 \sqrt{2} .]

sections.normalized_html: Find the length of the diagonal [MATH: \overline{AC}] of the square [MATH: ABCD] if the perimeter of the square is [MATH: p=256\,\mathrm{mm}.]
sections.readable_text: Find the length of the diagonal [MATH: \overline{AC}] of the square [MATH: ABCD] if the perimeter of the square is [MATH: p=256\,\mathrm{mm}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Since the perimeter is [MATH: p=256\,\textrm{mm},] the length of a single side is [MATH: AB = \dfrac{p}{4} = \dfrac{256}{4} = 64\,\mathrm{mm}.]

Now, consider [MATH: \triangle{ABC}], which is an isosceles right triangle since [MATH: \angle{ABC} = 90^\circ] and [MATH: AB=BC.]

The hypotenuse in an isosceles right triangle is equal to [MATH: \sqrt{2}] times the length of a leg.

Here, the length of a leg is [MATH: AB=64,] so the length of the hypotenuse is [MATH: AC = \sqrt{2}\cdot AB = \sqrt{2}\cdot 64 = 64\sqrt{2}\,\textrm{mm}.]

Therefore, the diagonal of the square [MATH: ABCD] has a length of [MATH: AC= 64 \sqrt{2} \, \textrm{mm}.]

Item 5 — Example: Calculating the Length of the Legs of a 45-45-90 Triangle Given the Hypotenuse

Example Prompt:
If the hypotenuse of a [MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 90^\circ] triangle has a length of [MATH: 5,] then what is the length of each leg?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The hypotenuse in a [MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 45^\circ]-[MATH: 90^\circ] triangle is equal to [MATH: \sqrt{2}] times the length of a leg.

Here, we know that the hypotenuse has length [MATH: 5.] So, if the length of a leg is [MATH: a,] then we must have

[MATH: 5|= sqrt(2) ⋅ a; a|= (5)/(sqrt(2)).]

To remove the square root from the denominator, we can multiply both the numerator and denominator by [MATH: \sqrt{2},] as follows:

[MATH: a|= (5 ⋅ sqrt(2))/(sqrt(2) ⋅ sqrt(2)); a|= (5sqrt(2))/(2)]

Therefore, the length of each leg is [MATH: \dfrac{5\sqrt{2}}{2}.]

Because the triangle is isosceles, the legs must have the same length. Let [MATH: a] be the length of each leg. So, we have

Moreover, because the triangle is a right isosceles triangle, the hypotenuse must be equal to [MATH: \sqrt{2}] times the length of a leg. Therefore,
[MATH: AC = AB\cdot\sqrt{2} = a\sqrt{2}.]

Finally, since the perimeter is [MATH: p = 26+13\sqrt{2},] we have

[MATH: p|= AB + BC + AC; 26 + 13sqrt(2)|= a + a + asqrt(2); 26 + 13sqrt(2)|= 2a + asqrt(2); 13(2 + sqrt(2))|= a(2 + sqrt(2)); 13(2 + sqrt(2))|= a(2 + sqrt(2)); 13|= a.]

Therefore, the length of each leg is [MATH: a=13,] and the length of the hypotenuse is

Now, consider [MATH: \triangle{ABC}], which is an isosceles right triangle since [MATH: \angle{ABC} = 90^\circ] and [MATH: AB=BC.]

[IMG: /graphics/d0d837d5a61929735e07c1a3ba172286]

Here, the length of a leg is [MATH: AB=64,] so the length of the hypotenuse is
[MATH: AC = \sqrt{2}\cdot AB = \sqrt{2}\cdot 64 = 64\sqrt{2}\,\textrm{mm}.]

Therefore, the diagonal of the square [MATH: ABCD] has a length of [MATH: AC= 64 \sqrt{2} \, \textrm{mm}.]
